Fifty comments

A Swedish Waltz from Vasen. Played very slow.

↳ Posted by injun bob on October 6th, 2002.

I’m not sure of the correct spelling, but this is the tune recorded on Dervish’s “At the End of the Day” as “Josefin’s.”

↳ Posted by slainte on October 6th, 2002.

Josefin’s Waltz by Roger Tallroth

The wildly popular contra dance band Swallowtail (based in Massachusetts) included it on their recording “After the Dance.” The liner notes say “Swedish guitarist Roger Tallroth composed this beautiful waltz for his niece’s christening.”

I also heard it played by Tallroth and his group (sorry, I don’t recall the name) on the Prairie Home Companion radio show.

↳ Posted by mvhplank on October 12th, 2002.

Josefin’s Waltz by Tallroth

This tune is on the CD Trio from the Swedish group Vasen with Tallroth. Go and listen, this is great music

↳ Posted by wolferen on October 18th, 2004.

↳ Posted by Heather MacLeod on August 1st, 2016.

Re: Josefin’s

I feel we should respect Tallroth’s original basic version of this tune (which you can hear and see him play with Väsen at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ZrfjHeFEr0). This means: 1) both A & B parts are repeated; 2) the last bar of the first time through A descends, leading back to the first pitch again (A-G-E if it’s played in G); 3) and two bars before the end of part A, it’s not E-F#-G but D-F#-G. Of course, then they (in all their concerts, and on the album “Trio”) vary it after that first AABB, so we can all have fun with it too. - Spelling too: Tallroth spells it “Johsefins Dopvals”.

Re: Josefin’s

This has been mentioned before a couple of times here but I just want to repeat it for emphasis - I hear this played wrong so often and it would be a shame for it to become the norm…
The ascending run up to the final “A” of the second line (if played in G) should be D F# G and not E F# G as written in many of these settings.
Don’t mean to be a pedant but it makes a difference as the two versions don’t sit well together harmonically if played simultaneously by different players in a session.
Have a listen to Väsen playing Roger Tallroth’s original …

Josefin’s, X:13

It appears that NONE of the above versions of this tune faithfully and completely reflect the playing of the band, Vasen, which includes the tune’s composer, Roger Tallroth, as heard on the two YouTube videos linked, https://youtu.be/_ZrfjHeFEr0 and https://youtu.be/SfUpGaPnZsA. I’ve listened to them both very carefully. They play it the same way, in F Major, in both videos (except for the improvisatory break). I am submitting what I hear in the videos, first in F major, as they play it, then in G major, where most others (including myself) play it.
